overall_summary: Analysis of 47 deduplicated video observations reveals a stark performance divergence. Second-person immersive space survival hooks—specifically the 'What If You Fell Into...' formula exploring extreme exoplanets—consistently generate the highest reach (800–1,050+ views) and strongest engagement (likes-per-view up to 3.7% with active comment sections). Conversely, abstract psychology trivia and recycled brain facts underperform severely (sub-100 views, near-zero engagement). Re-uploading identical hooks shows steep diminishing returns.

winning_patterns.pattern: Second-Person Immersive Cosmic Hazard ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes, 2 comments) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (974 views, 18 likes) dramatically outperform third-person trivia titles.
winning_patterns.action: Use visceral second-person sensory immersion focusing on the catastrophic physics of extreme space bodies.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice Will Break Your Brain!' (1,057 views, 3 comments), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,031 views, 36 likes), and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) hit top-tier benchmarks.
winning_patterns.action: Highlight mind-bending physical contradictions (e.g., solid matter under extreme heat, impossible atmospheric pressures) within the first 2 seconds.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' logged as low as 5 to 53 views across repeated attempts with 0 likes; 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' gathered only 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: Pause production on general brain/psychology facts unless framed through high-stakes survival or micro-mystery.

weak_patterns.pattern: Repetitive Topic Recycling Without Angle Shift
weak_patterns.evidence: 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' collapsed from 220 views to 87 and then 34 views across re-runs.
weak_patterns.action: Discontinue posting near-identical topics; mandate completely unique celestial bodies or phenomena.
